$comment: Claude Code settings for the container. Mounted READ-ONLY, so the agent
cannot disable its own guardrails even with permission prompts skipped.
The read-only bind mount is enforced by the kernel, which is why this does
Empirically verified on 2026-08-16: PreToolUse hooks still execute and
still block under --dangerously-skip-permissions. The published docs only
state that 'ask' rules survive bypass mode and are silent on hooks, so the
ask rules below are deliberate redundancy in case that behaviour changes.
The hook is the primary control because it normalizes the command first
and therefore also catches 'git -C <dir> push', which prefix-matched
statusLine points at the host's ~/.claude/statusline.sh, bind-mounted
volume cannot shadow it). Its dependencies -- bash, jq, awk, sed, stty, git
-- are all present in the image.
